title: Publish a complete 6-part video script series for TikTok and YouTube Shorts on cohort management
description: Short-form video is the primary channel where young educators, student community leaders, and bootcamp tutors discover new tools. Work under this goal: write 6 tight, 45-60 second educational video scripts covering common cohort problems (handling noisy WhatsApp groups, tracking homework submissions, running low-data voice check-ins, setting up channels by week). Each script includes visual hook directions, on-screen text overlays, and a clear call-to-action to try zedu.chat. Done when: 6 scripts with visual prompts and captions are delivered and approved.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Record the real screen action first, then write each script around what the footage shows
acceptedWorkstreams.description: For each of the six topics (noisy groups, homework tracking, low-data voice check-ins, channels by week and the others), a person records the actual steps in the live Zedu app first. The agent then writes the 45 to 60 second script, the on-screen text and the caption from what the footage really shows, so no feature is claimed that the video cannot show. Each script has a hook, the numbered steps with timings, the text overlays, a caption and one call to action to zedu.chat. No statistics or testimonials. Done when six scripts each match a recorded take, and the team confirms every step is true to the app.

upvotes.reason: Scripting from a real recording is a practical safeguard against promising screens or features the live app does not show. Matching each script to a confirmed take and avoiding unsupported stats makes the videos safer to publish.

pendingIdeas.title: Six scripts, six different problems: a source-checked coverage matrix so the series does not collapse into one WhatsApp video
pendingIdeas.description:
A six-part series usually repeats one problem six ways. This one starts from a coverage matrix, so each script earns its place.

Approach: (1) Build a six-row matrix - problem, who reports it, source link and date, the Zedu action shown on screen, and the one-line CTA. (2) Assign six distinct problems, not six angles on one: WhatsApp noise, homework/receipt tracking, low-data voice check-ins, week-by-week channel setup, late joiners catching up, and announcements getting buried. The last three come from verified operator posts collected on 22 Oct 2026 (20 posts, 14 LinkedIn + 6 X, each with a date and working link). (3) For each script write the three-second spoken hook naming the problem, the 45-60 second script, on-screen overlays, and the screen recording to capture in the live app. (4) Add one proof-shot line per script: the exact screen and tap that shows the fix, so nothing is claimed the product cannot show.

Fit: short-form video is how young educators discover tools, and six real problems give six entry points instead of one topic. Research is already done, every claim is traceable, and this stays inside Radar's lane.

Done when: six scripts are delivered, no two share the same underlying complaint, each cites its source post and date in an internal column (not on screen), and each has hook, overlays, CTA and proof-shot directions.

Measurement: show the hooks to three reviewers for "would you stop scrolling?" before filming; after posting, compare three-second hold and completion against the account baseline and count link clicks to zedu.chat per script. The matrix then shows which problem earns the most watch time, which sets the next series.

upvotes.reason: "Six scripts, six different problems: a source-checked coverage matrix so the series does not collapse into one WhatsApp video" has a scriptable structure, so it can be produced and reviewed rather than left open-ended. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

Six scripts built from one problem six ways is the default failure of a series. A coverage matrix with a source link and check date per row, drawn from verified operator posts, is checkable and keeps each script distinct.

Mapping six distinct cohort pain points (onboarding, drop-offs, assignment tracking, engagement, live sessions, graduation) prevents the short-form video series from becoming repetitive and ensures comprehensive coverage for prospective educators.

The accepted workstreams set the hook style and recording method but not what each episode covers. A six-row matrix of distinct, sourced problems keeps the series from repeating the WhatsApp angle six times.
